subproblems.title: Newtonian-potential solution of div ψ = a with a support-volume sup bound (replaces Simon 6, Remark 2.35)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. There is a constant C ∈ ℝ, depending only on m, with the following property. Let a : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, and let M ∈ ℝ satisfy |a(y)| ≤ M for every y ∈ ℝⁿ. Then there are C^∞ functions ψ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ Fin n) such that Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = a(y) for every y, where ∂_jψ_j(y) := Dψ_j(y)e_j and e_j is the j-th standard basis vector, and |ψ_j(y)| ≤ C·M·Lⁿ(spt a)^{1/n} for every j and y. Here spt a = tsupport a is the closed support of a and Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ = Eucl n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ y, |a y| ≤ M) → ∃ ψ : Fin (m + 1) → Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (ψ j)) ∧ (∀ y, ∑ j : Fin (m + 1), fderiv ℝ (ψ j) y (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) = a y) ∧ ∀ j y, |ψ j y| ≤ C * M * ((volume (tsupport a)).toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof, which replaces Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.35. It rests on the representation formula of D. Gilbarg and N. S. Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order, Lemma 7.14, and the elementary potential estimate of their §7.8. Throughout, n = m + 1 ≥ 1, |·| is the Euclidean norm on ℝⁿ, Lⁿ = volume, and B_ρ(y) is the open ball. We write |w|^{1−n} for (|w|^{n−1})^{−1}; in Lean this is (‖w‖^m)⁻¹, because the natural-number exponent 1 − n would truncate.

1. Constants and polar coordinates. Let ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞) and C := ((n+1)/n)·ω_n^{−1/n}; C depends only on m. Let σ := volume.toSphere be the surface measure on the unit sphere S^{n−1}. By Measure.toSphere_apply_univ, σ(S^{n−1}) = n·ω_n.
 Polar coordinates (P): for every g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ),
  ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(t) dt = ∫_{S^{n−1}} ∫_0^∞ r^{n−1} g(rθ) dr dσ(θ).
 This follows from Measure.measurePreserving_homeomorphUnitSphereProd, which carries Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ∖{0} to σ ⊗ r^{n−1}dr on S^{n−1} × (0, ∞), together with the fact that {0} is Lⁿ-null. The Lean ingredients are:
  – integral_subtype_comap with restrict_compl_singleton;
  – MeasurePreserving.integral_comp and MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb, for the measurable embedding of the homeomorphism;
  – integrableOn_iff_comap_subtypeVal;
  – integral_prod (Fubini);
  – integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul, to unfold the radial measure Measure.volumeIoiPow (n−1).
 Mathlib's proof of integral_fun_norm_addHaar is the template.
 For radial functions, integral_fun_norm_addHaar gives ∫ h(|w|) dw = n ω_n ∫_0^∞ r^{n−1} h(r) dr, and integrableOn_fun_norm_addHaar gives the matching integrability criterion. Hence, for every ρ > 0, w ↦ |w|^{1−n} is integrable on B_ρ(0), because its radial profile r^{n−1}·r^{1−n} = 1 is integrable on (0, ρ), and
  (R) ∫_{B_ρ(0)} |w|^{1−n} dw = n ω_n ∫_0^ρ 1 dr = n ω_n ρ.
 These formulas hold uniformly for every n ≥ 1, so no case distinction is needed; for n = 1, S⁰ = {±1} and n ω_n = 2.

2. The kernels. For j ∈ Fin n let K_j(w) := w_j/(n ω_n |w|ⁿ) for w ≠ 0 and K_j(0) := 0 (in Lean, division by 0 already gives 0). K_j is Borel measurable, and |K_j(w)| ≤ |w|^{1−n}/(n ω_n) because |w_j| ≤ |w|. By Step 1, |·|^{1−n} is integrable on every ball, so K_j is integrable on every ball by domination. Hence K_j is locally integrable.

3. Definition and smoothness of ψ_j. Fix a ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ) and M with |a| ≤ M everywhere. Put ψ_j := K_j ⋆ a, the convolution with the scalar multiplication pairing (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ): ψ_j(y) = ∫ K_j(t) a(y − t) dt (convolution_def). K_j is locally integrable and a is C^∞ with compact support, so ψ_j is C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right. Its derivative at y is (K_j ⋆ Da)(y) for the precomposed pairing (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right). Evaluating at e_k with convolution_precompR_apply gives, for every k,
  ∂_kψ_j(y) = ∫ K_j(t) ∂_k a(y − t) dt.

4. Representation formula: Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = a(y) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ. Fix y.
 (a) Ray FTC. Let θ be a unit vector and h(r) := a(y − rθ). Then h is C¹ with h′(r) = −Da(y − rθ)θ, and h(r) = 0 for all large r because a has compact support. By integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto,
  ∫_0^∞ Da(y − rθ)θ dr = h(0) − lim_{r→∞} h(r) = a(y).
 (b) Pointwise identity. Expanding t in the standard basis gives Da(y − t)t = Σ_j t_j ∂_j a(y − t). Hence, for t ≠ 0,
  Σ_j K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) = G(t) := Da(y − t)t/(n ω_n |t|ⁿ),
 and both sides are 0 at t = 0.
 (c) Integrability. Each t ↦ K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) is integrable, because K_j is locally integrable and ∂_j a is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_right). Therefore G is integrable and, by Step 3 with k = j, Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = Σ_j ∫ K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) dt = ∫ G(t) dt.
 (d) Apply (P) to G. For r > 0 and |θ| = 1,
  r^{n−1} G(rθ) = r^{n−1}·Da(y − rθ)(rθ)/(n ω_n rⁿ) = Da(y − rθ)θ/(n ω_n).
 By (a) the inner radial integral is a(y)/(n ω_n). Integrating this constant over S^{n−1} gives σ(S^{n−1})·a(y)/(n ω_n) = a(y). Hence Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = a(y).

5. The sup bound. Let S := tsupport a. It is compact, so Lⁿ(S) < ∞. Also M ≥ |a(0)| ≥ 0.
 Case Lⁿ(S) = 0. The open set {a ≠ 0} is contained in S, so it is Lⁿ-null. A nonempty open subset of ℝⁿ has positive Lebesgue measure, so this set is empty. Hence a ≡ 0 and ψ_j ≡ 0, and |ψ_j(y)| = 0 ≤ C·M·0^{1/n} = 0 (the exponent 1/n is positive).
 Case Lⁿ(S) > 0. Put ρ := (Lⁿ(S)/ω_n)^{1/n} > 0, so that Lⁿ(S) = ω_n ρⁿ. Fix y and let S_y := {t : y − t ∈ S}. The map t ↦ y − t preserves Lebesgue measure, so Lⁿ(S_y) = Lⁿ(S). Since a(y − t) = 0 for t ∉ S_y and |a| ≤ M, Step 2 gives
  |ψ_j(y)| ≤ ∫_{S_y} |K_j(t)|·|a(y − t)| dt ≤ (M/(n ω_n)) ∫_{S_y} |t|^{1−n} dt.
 Split S_y into S_y ∩ B_ρ(0) and S_y ∖ B_ρ(0).
 – By (R), ∫_{S_y ∩ B_ρ(0)} |t|^{1−n} dt ≤ n ω_n ρ.
 – On S_y ∖ B_ρ(0) we have |t| ≥ ρ, so |t|^{1−n} ≤ ρ^{1−n}. That part of the integral is therefore at most ρ^{1−n} Lⁿ(S_y) = ρ^{1−n} ω_n ρⁿ = ω_n ρ.
 Hence ∫_{S_y} |t|^{1−n} dt ≤ (n + 1) ω_n ρ, and
  |ψ_j(y)| ≤ (M/(n ω_n))·(n + 1) ω_n ρ = ((n+1)/n)·M·ω_n^{−1/n}·Lⁿ(S)^{1/n} = C·M·Lⁿ(S)^{1/n}.

6. Conclusion. The functions ψ_j of Step 3 are C^∞. They satisfy Σ_j ∂_jψ_j = a (Step 4) and |ψ_j(y)| ≤ C·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n} for all j and y (Step 5), with C from Step 1 independent of a and M. In the Lean statement, Lⁿ(tsupport a) is finite and equals (volume (tsupport a)).toReal, the exponent 1/((m:ℝ)+1) equals 1/n, and ∂_jψ_j(y) is fderiv ℝ (ψ j) y (EuclideanSpace.single j 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix ω_n = Lⁿ(B_1) and C = ((n+1)/n)ω_n^{−1/n}. Use polar coordinates, where σ(S^{n−1}) = nω_n, and the radial integral ∫_{B_ρ}|w|^{1−n} = nω_nρ.
The kernels K_j(w) = w_j/(nω_n|w|ⁿ) are locally integrable, with |K_j(w)| ≤ |w|^{1−n}/(nω_n).
ψ_j := K_j ⋆ a is C^∞, and ∂_kψ_j = K_j ⋆ ∂_k a (convolution with a compactly supported smooth function).
Representation Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = ∫ Da(y−t)t/(nω_n|t|ⁿ) dt = a(y), from polar coordinates centred at 0 and the FTC along the rays r ↦ y − rθ (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemma 7.14).
Sup bound: split y − spt a (same measure as spt a) at the radius ρ = (Lⁿ(spt a)/ω_n)^{1/n} to get |ψ_j| ≤ ((n+1)/n)Mρ = C·M·Lⁿ(spt a)^{1/n}. The case Lⁿ(spt a) = 0 forces a ≡ 0.

subproblems.title: Exterior derivative of the pulled-back potential form (Simon 6, 1.14 and the divergence identity of 2.35)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let L : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map, f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ψ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ for j ∈ Fin n, and x ∈ ℝ^P, such that f is differentiable at x and every ψ_j is differentiable at Lx. Let λ_i := y^i∘L for i ∈ Fin n, where y^i = EuclideanSpace.proj i is the i-th coordinate function of ℝⁿ. Let λ := λ_0∧⋯∧λ_m = wedgeCovectors n λ, and for j ∈ Fin n let θ_j := wedgeCovectors m (λ∘j.succAbove), the wedge of the λ_i with λ_j omitted. Let Φ be the (n−1)-form Φ(z) := Σ_j (−1)^j f(z) ψ_j(Lz) θ_j. Then its exterior derivative (Mathlib extDeriv) at x is dΦ(x) = f(x)(Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(Lx)) λ + Σ_j (−1)^j ψ_j(Lx)·wedgeCovectors n (Fin.cons (Df(x)) (λ∘j.succAbove)). Here ∂_jψ_j(Lx) := Dψ_j(Lx)e_j, and wedgeCovectors n (Fin.cons γ β) is the wedge γ∧β_0∧⋯∧β_{m−1}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 of the parent proof, written in coordinates. There, d(π^#ψ̂) = π^#(dψ̂) = (a∘π)Q^*dx^α by Simon Ch. 6, 1.14, and dψ̂ = (div ψ)dy as in Remark 2.35.
Indices i, j, k range over Fin n = {0, …, m}, and signs (−1)^j use the 0-based index. For 1-covectors β_0, …, β_r on ℝ^P write wedge(β) := wedgeCovectors (r+1) β. By SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det, wedge(β)(v_0, …, v_r) = det(β_k(v_l))_{k,l}. Let Alt denote ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin. Mathlib defines extDeriv ω x = Alt(Dω(x)). By the definition of wedgeCovectors, wedge(Fin.cons γ β) = Alt(γ.smulRight(wedge β)) for every 1-covector γ and every β : Fin m → 1-covectors.

1. Linearity in the first slot. Fix β : Fin m → (ℝ^P)^*. The map γ ↦ wedge(Fin.cons γ β) = Alt(γ.smulRight(wedge β)) is linear, because smulRight is linear in γ and Alt is linear (Alt = alternatizeUncurryFinCLM). Hence wedge(Fin.cons (Σ_i c_i γ_i) β) = Σ_i c_i·wedge(Fin.cons γ_i β).

2. Sign lemma. For every family λ : Fin n → (ℝ^P)^* and every j ∈ Fin n:
 (a) wedge(Fin.cons λ_j (λ∘j.succAbove)) = (−1)^j wedge(λ);
 (b) wedge(Fin.cons λ_i (λ∘j.succAbove)) = 0 for every i ≠ j.
 Proof of (a). Let σ := (Fin.cycleRange j)^{−1}. It is a permutation of Fin n with σ(0) = j and σ(k+1) = j.succAbove(k) (Mathlib Fin.cycleRange_symm_zero, Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ). Hence Fin.cons λ_j (λ∘j.succAbove) = λ∘σ. For every v, the matrix (λ_{σ(k)}(v_l))_{k,l} is the matrix (λ_k(v_l))_{k,l} with its rows permuted by σ, so its determinant is sign(σ)·det(λ_k(v_l)) (Matrix.det_permute). Now sign(σ) = sign(cycleRange j) = (−1)^j (Equiv.Perm.sign_symm, Fin.sign_cycleRange). By the determinant formula, (a) follows.
 Proof of (b). Since i ≠ j, there is k ∈ Fin m with j.succAbove(k) = i (Fin.exists_succAbove_eq). In the matrix of wedge(Fin.cons λ_i (λ∘j.succAbove))(v), rows 0 and k+1 both equal (λ_i(v_l))_l. So the determinant vanishes for every v (Matrix.det_zero_of_row_eq).

3. Derivative of Φ. For j ∈ Fin n put g_j(z) := (−1)^j f(z) ψ_j(Lz). L is linear and ψ_j is differentiable at Lx, so by the chain rule and the product rule g_j is differentiable at x, with
 Dg_j(x) = (−1)^j ( f(x)·(Dψ_j(Lx)∘L) + ψ_j(Lx)·Df(x) ).
 Since Φ(z) = Σ_j g_j(z) θ_j with constant θ_j, DΦ(x) = Σ_j Dg_j(x).smulRight θ_j. By linearity of Alt,
 dΦ(x) = Alt(DΦ(x)) = Σ_j Alt(Dg_j(x).smulRight θ_j) = Σ_j wedge(Fin.cons Dg_j(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)).

4. Coordinates of Dψ_j(Lx)∘L. For v ∈ ℝ^P write Lv = Σ_i (Lv)_i e_i in the standard basis of ℝⁿ. Then Dψ_j(Lx)(Lv) = Σ_i (Lv)_i Dψ_j(Lx)e_i = Σ_i ∂_iψ_j(Lx) λ_i(v). Hence Dψ_j(Lx)∘L = Σ_i ∂_iψ_j(Lx) λ_i as 1-covectors.

5. The divergence term. By Steps 1, 4 and 2,
 wedge(Fin.cons (Dψ_j(Lx)∘L) (λ∘j.succAbove)) = Σ_i ∂_iψ_j(Lx)·wedge(Fin.cons λ_i (λ∘j.succAbove)) = (−1)^j ∂_jψ_j(Lx)·wedge(λ).

6. Assembly. Apply Step 1 to the formula for Dg_j(x) in Step 3, then use Step 5 and (−1)^j(−1)^j = 1:
 wedge(Fin.cons Dg_j(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)) = (−1)^j f(x)(−1)^j ∂_jψ_j(Lx) wedge(λ) + (−1)^j ψ_j(Lx) wedge(Fin.cons Df(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)) = f(x) ∂_jψ_j(Lx) wedge(λ) + (−1)^j ψ_j(Lx) wedge(Fin.cons Df(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)).
 Summing over j and using Step 3,
 dΦ(x) = (f(x) Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(Lx))·wedge(λ) + Σ_j (−1)^j ψ_j(Lx)·wedge(Fin.cons Df(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)).
 This is the claim, since wedge(λ) = wedgeCovectors n (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i).comp L) and θ_j = wedgeCovectors m (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj (j.succAbove i)).comp L). ∎
proof_key_steps: dΦ(x) = Alt(DΦ(x)) and wedge(Fin.cons γ β) = Alt(γ.smulRight(wedge β)); this expression is linear in γ.
Sign lemma by determinants: wedge(Fin.cons λ_j (λ∘j.succAbove)) = (−1)^j wedge(λ), via the permutation (cycleRange j)^{−1}. With λ_i in front, i ≠ j, the wedge vanishes because of a repeated row.
Product and chain rule: Dg_j(x) = (−1)^j(f(x)·Dψ_j(Lx)∘L + ψ_j(Lx)·Df(x)), so dΦ(x) = Σ_j wedge(Fin.cons Dg_j(x) (λ∘j.succAbove)).
Dψ_j(Lx)∘L = Σ_i ∂_iψ_j(Lx)λ_i, so the f-terms collapse to f(x)·Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(Lx)·wedge(λ).

subproblems.title: Mass bound for test forms with bounded operator norm (Simon 6, 2.4–2.6)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n), and B, C ∈ ℝ. Assume 0 ≤ B, M_W(T) ≤ B (that is, T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B), tsupport ω ⊆ W, and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm of continuous alternating maps on ℝ^P with its Euclidean norm. Then |T(ω)| ≤ P^n·B·C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x‖ ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, which derives the mass bounds from the definition of M_W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5, with the norm of Remark 2.6). Here the comparison between the Euclidean coefficient norm |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm and the operator norm ‖·‖ is made explicit.

1. Comparison of norms. Let φ be an n-covector on ℝ^P and e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun k, so ‖e_k‖ = 1. By definition, |φ|² = Σ_I φ(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})², where the sum runs over the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; in the defining sum over all I : Fin n → Fin P, the other terms are 0. By the operator-norm inequality (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |φ(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖φ‖ Π_i ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖φ‖. There are P^n maps Fin n → Fin P, so |φ|² ≤ P^n‖φ‖². Hence |φ| ≤ √(P^n)·‖φ‖ ≤ P^n·‖φ‖, because P^n is a natural number k and √k ≤ k for every natural k (k = 0 or k ≥ 1).

2. Homogeneity. For t ∈ ℝ, |tφ| = (Σ_I t² φ(e_I)²)^{1/2} = |t|·|φ|.

3. Scaling. Eucl P is nonempty, so C ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. Put K₀ := P^n·C ≥ 0. Let s > 0 with s ≥ K₀, and let ε ∈ {1, −1}. The form η := (ε/s)·ω lies in Dⁿ(U), since Dⁿ(U) is a submodule. Also tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and for every x, Steps 2 and 1 give |η(x)| = s^{−1}|ω(x)| ≤ s^{−1}P^n‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s^{−1}K₀ ≤ 1. Hence η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. M_W(T) is a supremum over admissible forms (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), so ENNReal.ofReal(T(η)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(B). Since B ≥ 0, this gives T(η) ≤ B, that is, (ε/s)·T(ω) ≤ B by linearity of T. Taking ε = 1 and ε = −1 gives |T(ω)| ≤ s·B.

4. Conclusion. If K₀ > 0, take s = K₀: |T(ω)| ≤ K₀B = P^n·B·C. If K₀ = 0, then |T(ω)| ≤ sB for every s > 0, and letting s ↓ 0 gives |T(ω)| ≤ 0 = P^n·B·C. ∎
proof_key_steps: |φ| ≤ √(P^n)‖φ‖ ≤ P^n‖φ‖, because each coordinate satisfies |φ(e_I)| ≤ ‖φ‖ and there are P^n index maps.
Homogeneity |tφ| = |t||φ|.
For s > 0 with s ≥ P^nC, the forms ±ω/s are admissible for M_W, so ±T(ω)/s ≤ B, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ sB.
Take s = P^nC, or let s ↓ 0 when P^nC = 0.

subproblems.title: Potential bound for the top-dimensional functionals a ↦ T(f·(a∘L)·L^*dy) (Simon 6, proof of 2.36 with 2.35 replaced)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W ⊆ U, and let T ∈ D_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ W. Let L : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be continuous linear, and put L^*dy := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘L), where y^i is the i-th coordinate function of ℝⁿ. Then there is C ∈ ℝ with the following property. For every C^∞ compactly supported a : ℝⁿ → ℝ, every M ∈ ℝ with |a(y)| ≤ M for all y, and every test form φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ(x) = f(x)a(Lx)·L^*dy for all x, we have |T(φ)| ≤ C·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n}. Here Lⁿ(tsupport a) is the real number (volume (tsupport a)).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), W ⊆ U → T.massOn W < ∞ → T.boundary.massOn W < ∞ → ∀ f : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ W → ∀ L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ y, |a y| ≤ M) → ∀ φ : TestFormOn U (m + 1), (∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = (f x * a (L x)) • wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L)) → |T φ| ≤ C * M * ((volume (tsupport a)).toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 of the parent proof (its Claim and that Claim's proof), for a general linear map L in place of π_α = p_α∘Q.
Notation: λ_i := y^i∘L for i ∈ Fin n, and λ := wedgeCovectors n λ = L^*dy. For j ∈ Fin n, θ_j := wedgeCovectors m (λ∘j.succAbove) is an (n−1)-covector and η_j(x) := wedgeCovectors n (Fin.cons (Df(x)) (λ∘j.succAbove)) is an n-covector. ‖·‖ is the operator norm on covectors.

1. Constants. Let C₁ be the constant of the sibling potential_estimate for this m. Let F₀ := sup_x |f(x)| < ∞, finite because f is continuous with compact support. The map Λ_j : γ ↦ wedgeCovectors n (Fin.cons γ (λ∘j.succAbove)) = Alt(γ.smulRight θ_j) is a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional space of 1-covectors (Alt = alternatizeUncurryFin), and η_j(x) = Λ_j(Df(x)). Since f is C^∞, x ↦ Df(x) is continuous. It vanishes outside tsupport f, because f vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport f. Hence η_j is continuous with compact support, η_j(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport f, and H_j := sup_x ‖η_j(x)‖ < ∞. Let B₀ and B₁ be M_W(T) and M_W(∂T) as real numbers. Both are finite, so B₀, B₁ ≥ 0, M_W(T) ≤ ofReal B₀ and M_W(∂T) ≤ ofReal B₁. Define
 C := C₁·(P^m·B₁·F₀·Σ_j‖θ_j‖ + P^{m+1}·B₀·Σ_j H_j).
 C depends only on T, W, f and L.

2. The potential. Fix a, M and φ as in the statement. The sibling potential_estimate gives C^∞ functions ψ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ Fin n) with Σ_j ∂_jψ_j = a on ℝⁿ and |ψ_j(y)| ≤ R := C₁·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n} for all j and y. Note R ≥ |ψ_0(0)| ≥ 0.

3. The (n−1)-form Φ. Define Φ(z) := Σ_j (−1)^j f(z)ψ_j(Lz)·θ_j. Each coefficient z ↦ (−1)^j f(z)ψ_j(Lz) is C^∞, so Φ is C^∞. If f(z) = 0 then Φ(z) = 0, so support Φ ⊆ support f. Hence tsupport Φ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ W ⊆ U, and tsupport Φ is compact. So Φ ∈ D^m(U) = D^{n−1}(U).

4. dΦ = φ + Ξ. f is differentiable at every x and ψ_j at every Lx, and Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(Lx) = a(Lx). So the sibling potential_form_derivative gives, for every x,
 dΦ(x) = f(x)a(Lx)·λ + Σ_j (−1)^jψ_j(Lx)·η_j(x) = φ(x) + Σ_j (−1)^jψ_j(Lx)·η_j(x).
 dΦ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m Φ is a test form, and Dⁿ(U) is a vector space, so Ξ := dΦ − φ ∈ Dⁿ(U). For every x, Ξ(x) = Σ_j (−1)^jψ_j(Lx)·η_j(x). In particular Ξ(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport f, so tsupport Ξ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ W.

5. Splitting. Since φ = dΦ − Ξ and T is linear, T(φ) = T(dΦ) − T(Ξ) = ∂T(Φ) − T(Ξ), where ∂T(Φ) = T(dΦ) by the definition of ∂T.

6. Pointwise bounds. For every z,
 ‖Φ(z)‖ ≤ Σ_j |f(z)|·|ψ_j(Lz)|·‖θ_j‖ ≤ F₀·R·Σ_j‖θ_j‖, and
 ‖Ξ(z)‖ ≤ Σ_j |ψ_j(Lz)|·‖η_j(z)‖ ≤ R·Σ_j H_j.

7. Mass bounds. Apply the sibling mass_bound_opnorm to the m-current ∂T, the test form Φ (tsupport Φ ⊆ W) and B₁: |∂T(Φ)| ≤ P^m·B₁·F₀·R·Σ_j‖θ_j‖. Apply it to T, Ξ (tsupport Ξ ⊆ W) and B₀: |T(Ξ)| ≤ P^{m+1}·B₀·R·Σ_j H_j.

8. Conclusion. By Steps 5 and 7,
 |T(φ)| ≤ |∂T(Φ)| + |T(Ξ)| ≤ R·(P^m B₁ F₀ Σ_j‖θ_j‖ + P^{m+1} B₀ Σ_j H_j) = C·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix constants that do not depend on a: C₁ from potential_estimate, F₀ = sup|f|, H_j = sup_x‖Df(x)∧θ_j‖ (continuous with compact support), B₀ = M_W(T) and B₁ = M_W(∂T).
Take ψ from potential_estimate: Σ_j∂_jψ_j = a and |ψ_j| ≤ R = C₁·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n}.
Φ := Σ_j(−1)^j f·(ψ_j∘L)·θ_j is a test (n−1)-form with tsupport Φ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ W.
potential_form_derivative gives dΦ = φ + Ξ with Ξ = Σ_j(−1)^j(ψ_j∘L)·(Df∧θ_j), and tsupport Ξ ⊆ W.
T(φ) = ∂T(Φ) − T(Ξ). Bound both terms with mass_bound_opnorm, using ‖Φ‖ ≤ F₀RΣ_j‖θ_j‖ and ‖Ξ‖ ≤ RΣ_jH_j.

subproblems.title: Expansion of covectors in the rotated basis Q^*dx^α (Simon 6, §1 and proof of 2.36)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every linear isometry Q of ℝ^P and every n-covector φ on ℝ^P, φ = Σ_{α∈I(n,P)} φ(Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(n−1)})·Q^*dx^α. Here I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the set of strictly increasing maps Fin n → Fin P, e_k is the k-th standard basis vector of ℝ^P, and Q^*dx^α := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => x^{α(i)}∘Q) is the wedge of the 1-covectors x ↦ (Qx)_{α(i)}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Eucl P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Eucl P) (φ : Covector (Eucl P) n), φ = ∑ α : SimonMultiIndex n P, φ (fun i => Q.symm (EuclideanSpace.single (α i) (1 : ℝ))) • wedgeCovectors n (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj (α i) : Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp (Q : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the expansion ω = Σ_α ω_α dx^α at the start of Simon's proof of Lemma 2.36, in the coordinates of Simon Ch. 6, §1, run for Q_#T as in Remark 2.37(2); this is Step 1 of the parent proof.
Notation: for a tuple J : Fin n → Fin P write e_J := (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}). For α ∈ I(n,P) write dx^α := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => x^{α(i)}), where x^k = EuclideanSpace.proj k. By SimonGMT wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^α(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) = det((v_l)_{α(k)})_{k,l}.

1. Kronecker property. For α, γ ∈ I(n,P), dx^α(e_γ) = det(δ_{α(k),γ(l)})_{k,l}.
 – If α = γ, this matrix is the identity because α is injective, so dx^α(e_α) = 1.
 – If α ≠ γ, then range α ≠ range γ, since a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the increasing enumeration of its range and is determined by it. Both ranges have n elements, so some α(k) ∉ range γ. Row k of the matrix is then zero, and dx^α(e_γ) = 0.

2. Standard expansion. Let φ be an n-covector and ψ := Σ_{α∈I(n,P)} φ(e_α)·dx^α. By Step 1, ψ(e_γ) = Σ_α φ(e_α)·dx^α(e_γ) = φ(e_γ) for every γ ∈ I(n,P).
 Now let J : Fin n → Fin P be arbitrary.
 – If J is not injective, e_J has two equal entries, and φ(e_J) = 0 = ψ(e_J) because both maps are alternating.
 – If J is injective, let γ ∈ I(n,P) be the increasing enumeration of range J. Then J = γ∘σ for a permutation σ of Fin n (sort J, e.g. with Mathlib's Tuple.sort). Since φ and ψ are alternating, φ(e_J) = sign(σ)φ(e_γ) = sign(σ)ψ(e_γ) = ψ(e_J).
 So φ and ψ agree on all tuples of standard basis vectors. Multilinear maps that agree on all tuples of basis vectors are equal: expand each argument in the basis (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the alternating maps underlying φ and ψ). Hence φ = Σ_α φ(e_α)·dx^α. If n > P, then I(n,P) = ∅ and every J is non-injective, so φ = 0, which is consistent with the empty sum.

3. Rotated expansion. Let Q be a linear isometry; in particular Q is a linear bijection and Q^{−1} = Q.symm. Define the n-covector φ' := φ∘(Q^{−1})^{×n}, i.e. φ'(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) := φ(Q^{−1}v_0, …, Q^{−1}v_{n−1}); this is the pull-back covectorPullback n Q^{−1} φ. By Step 2,
 φ' = Σ_α φ'(e_α)·dx^α = Σ_α φ(Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(n−1)})·dx^α.
 For every v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) we have φ(v) = φ'(Qv_0, …, Qv_{n−1}), since Q^{−1}Qv_l = v_l. Hence
 φ(v) = Σ_α φ(Q^{−1}e_α)·dx^α(Qv_0, …, Qv_{n−1}).
 Finally, dx^α(Qv_0, …, Qv_{n−1}) = det((Qv_l)_{α(k)})_{k,l} = det((x^{α(k)}∘Q)(v_l))_{k,l} = Q^*dx^α(v), by wedgeCovectors_apply_det applied to both wedges (equivalently, SimonGMT covectorPullback_wedgeCovectors). Therefore φ = Σ_α φ(Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(n−1)})·Q^*dx^α. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^α(e_γ) = δ_{αγ} for increasing α and γ: the determinant of a partial permutation matrix.
Standard expansion φ = Σ_α φ(e_α)dx^α. Both sides are alternating and agree on increasing basis tuples. By sorting they agree on all basis tuples, hence everywhere.
Apply the standard expansion to φ' = φ∘(Q^{−1})^{×n} and pull back by Q, using dx^α(Qv) = Q^*dx^α(v).

subproblems.title: Smooth cutoffs equal to 1 on a compact Lebesgue-null set, with supports of small measure (Simon 6, proof of 2.36, display (2))
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let F ⊆ ℝ^N be compact with L^N(F) = 0 (L^N = volume on Eucl N), and let δ > 0. Then there is a C^∞ function b : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support such that 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, b = 1 on F, and L^N(tsupport b) ≤ δ, that is, (volume (tsupport b)).toReal ≤ δ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (F : Set (Eucl N)), IsCompact F → (volume : Measure (Eucl N)) F = 0 → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ b : Eucl N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧ (∀ y, 0 ≤ b y ∧ b y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ y ∈ F, b y = 1) ∧ ((volume : Measure (Eucl N)) (tsupport b)).toReal ≤ δ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the cutoff construction in Step 5 of the parent proof. Notation: dist(y, F) = infDist y F and G_ε := {y : dist(y, F) < ε} = thickening ε F.

0. If F = ∅, then b := 0 works, since tsupport 0 = ∅. Assume F ≠ ∅ from now on.

1. Small neighbourhoods. Each G_ε (ε > 0) is open and bounded (F is bounded), and G_ε ⊆ G_{ε'} for ε ≤ ε'. F is closed, so ⋂_{k≥1} G_{1/k} = closure F = F. Since L^N(G_1) < ∞, continuity of measure from above gives L^N(G_{1/k}) → L^N(F) = 0; this is Mathlib's tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed. Fix ε := 1/k > 0 with L^N(G_ε) ≤ δ.

2. Mollifier. Let φ_ε ∈ C^∞(ℝ^N) with φ_ε ≥ 0, ∫φ_ε = 1 and support φ_ε ⊆ B_{ε/4}(0); for example, the normalized smooth bump function ContDiffBump.normed with centre 0, inner radius ε/8 and outer radius ε/4.

3. Definition. Put b(y) := (1_{G_{ε/2}} ⋆ φ_ε)(y) = ∫ 1_{G_{ε/2}}(t)·φ_ε(y − t) dt = ∫ 1_{G_{ε/2}}(y − z)·φ_ε(z) dz. The indicator 1_{G_{ε/2}} is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable, and φ_ε is C^∞ with compact support. So b is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right).

4. Range. Since 0 ≤ 1_{G_{ε/2}} ≤ 1, φ_ε ≥ 0 and ∫φ_ε = 1, we have 0 ≤ b(y) ≤ 1.

5. b = 1 on F. Let y ∈ F and |z| < ε/4. Then dist(y − z, F) ≤ |z| < ε/2, so 1_{G_{ε/2}}(y − z) = 1 wherever φ_ε(z) ≠ 0. Hence b(y) = ∫φ_ε = 1.

6. Support. Suppose dist(y, F) ≥ 3ε/4. For |z| < ε/4 we get dist(y − z, F) ≥ dist(y, F) − |z| > ε/2, so 1_{G_{ε/2}}(y − z) = 0 wherever φ_ε(z) ≠ 0, and b(y) = 0. Thus support b ⊆ {dist(·, F) < 3ε/4}, and tsupport b ⊆ {dist(·, F) ≤ 3ε/4} ⊆ G_ε. The set tsupport b is closed and bounded, hence compact, so b has compact support.

7. Measure. L^N(tsupport b) ≤ L^N(G_ε) ≤ δ < ∞, so (volume (tsupport b)).toReal ≤ δ.

Remark (an equivalent route that may replace Steps 2–6). By outer regularity, choose an open G ⊇ F with L^N(G) < δ. Choose an open V with F ⊆ V ⊆ closure V ⊆ G and closure V compact (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure). Take a C^∞ function b : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with b = 1 on F and b = 0 on ℝ^N ∖ V (exists_contMDiffMap_zero_one_of_isClosed, then contMDiff_iff_contDiff). Then tsupport b ⊆ closure V ⊆ G. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose ε with L^N({dist(·, F) < ε}) ≤ δ, by continuity from above (F is compact and Lebesgue-null).
b := 1_{G_{ε/2}} ⋆ φ_ε, with a mollifier φ_ε supported in B_{ε/4}; b is C^∞ and 0 ≤ b ≤ 1.
b = 1 on F, and tsupport b ⊆ {dist(·, F) ≤ 3ε/4} ⊆ G_ε is compact, so L^N(tsupport b) ≤ δ.

subproblems.title: M_W(T) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for a compact K with null rotated projections (Simon 6, proof of 2.36, displays (1)–(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and T ∈ D_n(U) with M_W(T) + M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) be such that (IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) the function x ↦ ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dμ(x). Assume also that Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1 for μ-a.e. x. Let Q be a linear isometry of ℝ^P, and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with Lⁿ(π_α(K)) = 0 for every α ∈ I(n,P), where π_α(x) := ((Qx)_{α(0)}, …, (Qx)_{α(m)}). Then there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that M_W(T) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for every open W ⊂⊂ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → T.massOn W + T.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → ∀ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex (m + 1) P, (euclideanNVectorCoordinate (ξ x) β) ^ 2 = 1) → ∀ (Q : Eucl P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Eucl P) (K : Set (Eucl P)), IsCompact K → (∀ α : SimonMultiIndex (m + 1) P, (volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))) ((fun x : Eucl P => (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin (m + 1) => Q x (α i)) : Eucl (m + 1))) '' K) = 0) → ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → T.massOn W ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W \ K)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, displays (1)–(3), run for Q_#T as in Remark 2.37(2); this is Steps 4–5 of the parent proof. The currents p_{α#}(T⌞ω_α) are realized by the functionals a ↦ T(ω_α·(a∘π_α)·Q^*dx^α), and Remark 2.35 is replaced by the sibling pullback_top_form_bound. Printed (3) only needs some constant, so the orthonormality of Step 1 of the parent proof is not needed: explicit finite constants are used instead.
Notation: I := I(n,P). For α ∈ I let e^Q_α := (Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(m)}) and e_α := (e_{α(0)}, …, e_{α(m)}), let dx^α := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => x^{α(i)}), and let θ_α := Q^*dx^α = wedgeCovectors n (fun i => x^{α(i)}∘Q). |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. The pairing ⟨φ, ξ(x)⟩ is ξ(x)(φ), and euclideanNVectorCoordinate (ξ x) β = ξ(x)(dx^β).

1. The linear maps π_α. For α ∈ I let π_α : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be the continuous linear map x ↦ ((Qx)_{α(0)}, …, (Qx)_{α(m)}); it is the map in the hypothesis. For every i, y^i∘π_α = x^{α(i)}∘Q, so wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘π_α) = θ_α. The set F_α := π_α(K) is compact, and Lⁿ(F_α) = 0 by hypothesis.

2. Two expansions. By the sibling covector_rotated_expansion, every n-covector φ satisfies φ = Σ_{α∈I} φ(e^Q_α)·θ_α. With Q = identity, the same sibling gives φ = Σ_{β∈I} φ(e_β)·dx^β.

3. Coordinate bound. For every n-covector φ and β ∈ I, |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ|. Indeed, the strictly increasing map β is one of the indices of the sum |φ|² = Σ_{J strictly increasing} φ(e_J)², and all terms are ≥ 0.

4. Constants. For α ∈ I put c_α := Σ_{β∈I} |dx^β(e^Q_α)| and c'_α := Σ_{β∈I} |θ_α(e_β)|. Put C := 1 + Σ_{α∈I} c_α·c'_α ≥ 1. These depend only on P, n and Q.
 (a) If |φ| ≤ 1 then |φ(e^Q_α)| ≤ c_α. By Step 2 with Q = id, φ(e^Q_α) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(e^Q_α), and |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| ≤ 1 by Step 3.
 (b) For μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α for all α. By Step 2 with Q = id, θ_α = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·dx^β, so ξ(x)(θ_α) = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·ξ(x)(dx^β) by linearity of ξ(x). At every x with Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1, which holds for μ-a.e. x, each |ξ(x)(dx^β)| ≤ 1, so |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α.

5. Reduction. Fix an open W ⊂⊂ U. Then W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U, and M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ because their sum is finite. W∖K is Borel. If μ(W∖K) = ∞, then C·μ(W∖K) = ∞ because C > 0, and there is nothing to prove. Assume D := μ(W∖K) < ∞. M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over the admissible ω, i.e. those with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to show T(ω) ≤ (Σ_α c_α c'_α)·D for each admissible ω; then ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ofReal(C·D) = C·μ(W∖K).

6. Printed (1): decomposition. Fix an admissible ω and α ∈ I, and let ω_α(x) := ω(x)(e^Q_α).
 – Evaluation at the fixed tuple e^Q_α is a continuous linear map on covectors, so ω_α is C^∞.
 – ω_α(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0, so tsupport ω_α ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W and ω_α has compact support.
 – |ω_α| ≤ c_α by Step 4(a).
 The form ζ_α(x) := ω_α(x)·θ_α is a test form in Dⁿ(U). By Step 2, ω(x) = Σ_α ω_α(x)·θ_α for every x, i.e. ω = Σ_α ζ_α. By linearity, T(ω) = Σ_α T(ζ_α).

7. Printed (2): the estimate |T(ζ_α)| ≤ c_α c'_α D. Apply the sibling pullback_top_form_bound to T and W (W ⊆ U, finite masses), f := ω_α and L := π_α; it yields a constant C_α. Let δ > 0. The sibling null_compact_cutoff, applied to the compact null set F_α ⊆ ℝⁿ, gives a C^∞ compactly supported b : ℝⁿ → [0, 1] with b = 1 on F_α and Lⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ. Define the test forms φ₁(x) := ω_α(x)b(π_αx)·θ_α and φ₂ := ζ_α − φ₁, so φ₂(x) = ω_α(x)(1 − b(π_αx))·θ_α. φ₁ is C^∞ with tsupport φ₁ ⊆ tsupport ω_α ⊆ W ⊆ U. Then T(ζ_α) = T(φ₁) + T(φ₂).
 (a) By Step 1, φ₁(x) = ω_α(x)b(π_αx)·wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘π_α). So pullback_top_form_bound with a := b and M := 1 gives |T(φ₁)| ≤ C_α·Lⁿ(tsupport b)^{1/n} ≤ max(C_α, 0)·δ^{1/n}.
 (b) By the representation, T(φ₂) = ∫ g dμ with g(x) := ξ(x)(φ₂(x)) = ω_α(x)(1 − b(π_αx))·ξ(x)(θ_α), and g is μ-integrable. For μ-a.e. x, |g(x)| ≤ c_α c'_α·1_{W∖K}(x):
  – if x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω_α, so ω_α(x) = 0;
  – if x ∈ K, then π_αx ∈ F_α, so b(π_αx) = 1;
  – otherwise |g(x)| ≤ |ω_α(x)|·|1 − b(π_αx)|·|ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c_α·1·c'_α, by Step 6 and Step 4(b).
 Hence |T(φ₂)| ≤ ∫|g| dμ ≤ c_α c'_α·μ(W∖K) = c_α c'_α D.
 So |T(ζ_α)| ≤ max(C_α, 0)·δ^{1/n} + c_α c'_α D for every δ > 0. Letting δ ↓ 0, so that δ^{1/n} → 0, gives |T(ζ_α)| ≤ c_α c'_α D.

8. Printed (3). By Steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_α T(ζ_α) ≤ Σ_α |T(ζ_α)| ≤ (Σ_α c_α c'_α)·D. By Step 5, M_W(T) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and C does not depend on W. If I = ∅ (P < n), the sum is empty, T(ω) = 0, and the claim still holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: π_α is linear with y^i∘π_α = x^{α(i)}∘Q, so its top form is θ_α = Q^*dx^α. F_α = π_α(K) is compact and Lⁿ-null.
covector_rotated_expansion gives ω = Σ_α ω_α·θ_α, where ω_α = ω(Q^{−1}e_α) is smooth, supported in W, and |ω_α| ≤ c_α. With Q = id it gives |ξ(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α μ-a.e.
Split ζ_α = ω_α·θ_α using a cutoff b from null_compact_cutoff. Then |T(ω_α(b∘π_α)θ_α)| ≤ C_α·δ^{1/n} by pullback_top_form_bound.
The remainder equals ∫ω_α(1 − b∘π_α)ξ(θ_α) dμ. Its integrand vanishes off W and on K, so it is at most c_αc'_α·μ(W∖K).
Let δ → 0, sum over α, and take the supremum over admissible ω: M_W(T) ≤ C·μ(W∖K).

subproblems.title: Shrinking neighbourhoods: μ(W) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for all W ⊂⊂ U forces μ(K) = 0 (Simon 6, proof of 2.36 after (4))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let K ⊆ U be compact, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(W) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and let C ∈ [0, ∞) be such that μ(W) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then μ(K) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (C : ℝ≥0), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → μ W < ∞) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → μ W ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W \ K)) → μ K = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, the step after display (4) ("we can choose {W_q} so that W_q ⊂⊂ U, W_{q+1} ⊂ W_q, ⋂ W_q = K"). This is the last paragraph of Step 5 of the parent proof. W ⊂⊂ U means CompactlyContainedOpen W U: W is open, closure W is compact, and closure W ⊆ U.

1. K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is r₀ > 0 with cthickening r₀ K = {x : dist(x, K) ≤ r₀} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).

2. For q ∈ ℕ let r_q := r₀/(q+1) and W_q := {x : dist(x, K) < r_q} = thickening r_q K. Each W_q is open. Also closure W_q ⊆ cthickening r_q K ⊆ cthickening r₀ K ⊆ U. The set cthickening r_q K is compact (K is compact and ℝ^P is proper), so closure W_q is compact. Hence W_q ⊂⊂ U. The W_q decrease in q, and K ⊆ W_q for every q.

3. ⋂_q W_q = closure K = K. If dist(x, K) < r_q for all q, then dist(x, K) = 0, so x ∈ closure K = K because K is closed. Conversely K ⊆ W_q for every q.

4. The sets W_q∖K are Borel (open minus closed) and decrease in q. Also μ(W_0∖K) ≤ μ(W_0) < ∞, and ⋂_q (W_q∖K) = (⋂_q W_q)∖K = ∅. By continuity of measure from above, μ(W_q∖K) → 0.

5. For every q, K ⊆ W_q, so μ(K) ≤ μ(W_q) ≤ C·μ(W_q∖K). C is finite, so the right side tends to C·0 = 0. Hence μ(K) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick r₀ > 0 such that the closed r₀-neighbourhood of K lies in U.
W_q = {dist(·, K) < r₀/(q+1)} are open, ⊂⊂ U and decreasing, with ⋂_q W_q = K.
Continuity from above gives μ(W_q∖K) → 0. Then μ(K) ≤ μ(W_q) ≤ C·μ(W_q∖K) → 0.

subproblems.title: Inner regularity: a Borel set whose compact subsets in U are all μ-null is μ-null (Simon 1.15; 6, Remark 2.37(1))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0 and μ(W) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Let E ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set such that μ(K) = 0 for every compact K with K ⊆ E and K ⊆ U. Then μ(E) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U E : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → μ W < ∞) → MeasurableSet E → (∀ K, IsCompact K → K ⊆ E → K ⊆ U → μ K = 0) → μ E = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, the last lines of the proof of Lemma 2.36 and Remark 2.37(1), which use Ch. 1, 1.15(2). This is Step 6 of the parent proof. W ⊂⊂ U means CompactlyContainedOpen W U.

1. A countable cover of U by sets ⊂⊂ U. For x ∈ U choose ε_x > 0 with B(x, ε_x) ⊆ U, and put V_x := B(x, ε_x/2). V_x is open, and closure V_x ⊆ closedBall(x, ε_x/2) ⊆ B(x, ε_x) ⊆ U. By Heine–Borel, closedBall(x, ε_x/2) is compact, so closure V_x is compact and V_x ⊂⊂ U. The sets V_x (x ∈ U) cover U, and ℝ^P is second countable. By the Lindelöf property (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable) there is a countable set S ⊆ U with U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈S} V_x.

2. Each piece is null. Fix x ∈ S and let V := V_x. The restriction ν := μ⌞V is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(V) < ∞. So it is (weakly) regular: for every Borel set A, ν(A) = sup{ν(F) : F ⊆ A closed} (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(2); Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_lt_add for the WeaklyRegular finite measure ν). Apply this to the Borel set A := E ∩ V. Every closed F ⊆ E ∩ V is a closed subset of the compact set closure V, hence compact, and F ⊆ E and F ⊆ V ⊆ U. By hypothesis μ(F) = 0, so ν(F) ≤ μ(F) = 0. Therefore ν(E ∩ V) = 0. Since ν(E ∩ V) = μ(E ∩ V ∩ V) = μ(E ∩ V), we get μ(E ∩ V_x) = 0.

3. Conclusion. E ∩ U ⊆ ⋃_{x∈S} (E ∩ V_x) is contained in a countable union of μ-null sets, so μ(E ∩ U) = 0. Finally, μ(E) ≤ μ(E ∩ U) + μ(E∖U) ≤ 0 + μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many balls V_x ⊂⊂ U (Lindelöf property).
μ⌞V_x is finite, hence inner regular by closed sets. Closed subsets of E ∩ V_x are compact subsets of E ∩ U, so μ(E ∩ V_x) = 0.
Countable subadditivity and μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0 give μ(E) = 0.
